memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He then presented the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head. Moses slaughtered the bull and took some of the blood, and with his finger he put it on all the horns of the altar to purify the altar. He poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar. So he consecrated it to make atonement for it." - Lev 8:14-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Before Aaron can offer a single sacrifice for anyone else, a sacrifice must be offered for him.

He lays his hands on the bull's head — the same gesture any Israelite farmer would make. The high priest of the nation begins his ministry by admitting he is a sinner.

Hebrews draws out the difference between him and Christ with real force: he has to offer sacrifices... first for his own sins, and then for the sins of the people. He sacrificed for their sins once for all when he offered himself (Heb 7:27).

Every human minister of God begins where Aaron began. No one stands before God on the strength of their office.

There is also something striking about the altar itself needing purification. Even the furniture of worship, newly made and never used, required atoning blood. Nothing in a fallen world is automatically fit for God's presence.

This should keep us humble about our churches, our traditions, our ministries. None of them are holy by construction. They are holy only by God's cleansing and God's claim.

If you serve others spiritually in any way — as a parent, teacher, leader, friend — remember Aaron's hands on that head. Deal with your own sin first.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I attend to my own sin as carefully as I notice others'?
2. Am I serving others out of an honest walk with God, or out of position?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, before I serve anyone else, deal with me. Cleanse my own heart so that what I offer others is real. Amen.
